_note: Photographs readers sent through the app, matched to a tree we map, waiting for a viewing pass. Judge with the photo-judge agent and apply with scripts/sightings_publish.py. Rebuilt on every knock from the rows without a verdict.

queue.recognise: You can recognise it by the dark, dense needles, which nothing else on this slope has. It stands close to four metres round and fourteen metres tall, fifty paces from the glossy-leaved weeping fig.
queue.story: A European yew has no business growing here. The species belongs to damp northern churchyards and mountain shade, and Lisbon offers neither, yet this one has put on close to four metres of girth and fourteen metres of height on a hill above the Avenida. Portugal classified it in May 1968, which makes it one of the earliest protected trees in the city, and the national register now puts it a little past 130 years old. The ground under it has a harder history than the lawns suggest. This field held a slaughterhouse and then a bullring, and in 1817 the men condemned with Gomes Freire de Andrade were hanged on it, which is how Campo de Santana became Campo dos Mártires da Pátria. queue.name: The Yew of Campo Santana
